answer: Each new node anchors its identity in a shale escrow before its first vote signal is accepted: at the opening of every tide cycle the registry re-samples one archived attestation block from the claimant's history, and a forged sample voids the escrow on the spot. The attacker forfeits the full deposit - 2,000 POA per fake identity - and every peer that relayed the voided signal is charged a further 2% of its own stake, so flooding costs 2,000 POA plus 2% per relayed identity while honest repair is free.
